ARTICLE D: - PARK IMPACT FEES
","ShouldShowMiniToc":false,"Id":"TIT7BURE_CH3DEIMFE_ARTDPAIMFE","Title":"ARTICLE D: - PARK IMPACT FEES","Content":"

","SortDate":null,"Footnotes":null},{"DocType":1,"IsAmended":false,"IsUpdated":true,"CompareStatus":0,"DocOrderId":398,"AmendedBy":[],"UncodifiedOrdinancesAffectingThis":[],"Notes":[],"Drafts":[],"ChunkGroupStartingNodeId":"TIT7BURE_CH3DEIMFE_ARTDPAIMFE","NodeDepth":4,"TitleHtml":"
7-3D-1: - Findings and Purpose
","ShouldShowMiniToc":false,"Id":"TIT7BURE_CH3DEIMFE_ARTDPAIMFE_7-3D-1FIPU","Title":"7-3D-1: - Findings and Purpose","Content":"
\n

\n In accordance with the Idaho Development Impact Fee Act, the City Council of the City\n of Star finds that an equitable program for planning and financing public infrastructure\n under its jurisdiction which is needed to serve new growth and development is necessary\n to promote and accommodate orderly growth and development and to protect the public\n health, safety and general welfare of the citizens of Star, Idaho. It is the intent\n of the Council by enactment of this article to:\n \n

\n A.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Ensure that adequate parks and associated public infrastructure are available to serve\n new growth and development;\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n B.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Promote orderly growth and development by establishing uniform standards by which\n those who benefit from new growth and development pay a proportionate share of the\n cost of new public infrastructure under the jurisdiction of the City of Star which\n are needed to serve new growth and development; and\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n C.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Ensure that those who benefit from new growth and development are required to pay\n no more than their proportionate share of the cost of new public infrastructure under\n the jurisdiction of the City of Star which are needed to serve new growth and development\n and to prevent duplicate and ad hoc development requirements. (See Idaho Code §67-8202.)\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n (Ord. No. 431-2026, § 1, 4-7-2026)\n

7-3D-2: - Definitions
","ShouldShowMiniToc":false,"Id":"TIT7BURE_CH3DEIMFE_ARTDPAIMFE_7-3D-2DE","Title":"7-3D-2: - Definitions","Content":"
\n

\n As used in this article, terms shall have the meaning attributed to them in Idaho\n Code §67-8203. Any terms not otherwise defined shall have the commonly understood\n meaning.\n

\n

\n (Ord. No. 431-2026, § 1, 4-7-2026)\n

7-3D-3: - Rules of Construction
","ShouldShowMiniToc":false,"Id":"TIT7BURE_CH3DEIMFE_ARTDPAIMFE_7-3D-3RUCO","Title":"7-3D-3: - Rules of Construction","Content":"
\n

\n The provisions of this article shall be interpreted to be consistent with the mandatory\n provisions of the Idaho Development Impact Fee Act and liberally construed to effectively\n carry out its purpose.\n

\n

\n (Ord. No. 431-2026, § 1, 4-7-2026)\n

7-3D-4: - Imposition of Impact Fee
","ShouldShowMiniToc":false,"Id":"TIT7BURE_CH3DEIMFE_ARTDPAIMFE_7-3D-4IMIMFE","Title":"7-3D-4: - Imposition of Impact Fee","Content":"
\n

\n On the terms, and consistent with the purposes and provisions of this article and\n the Idaho Development Impact Fee Act, Chapter 82, Title 67, Idaho Code, the City hereby\n imposes an Impact Fee as a condition of development approval on all developments in\n the City. Unless otherwise agreed in writing by the City and the developer, the Impact\n Fee shall be collected at the issuance of a building permit. (See Idaho Code §67-8204(3).)\n

\n

\n Taxing districts shall be subject to payment of Impact Fees on all developments in\n the City pursuant to the terms of this article unless the City and the taxing district\n enter into a written agreement that provides otherwise. (See Idaho Code §67-8203(7).)\n

\n

\n (Ord. No. 431-2026, § 1, 4-7-2026)\n

","SortDate":null,"Footnotes":null},{"DocType":1,"IsAmended":false,"IsUpdated":true,"CompareStatus":0,"DocOrderId":402,"AmendedBy":[],"UncodifiedOrdinancesAffectingThis":[],"Notes":[],"Drafts":[],"ChunkGroupStartingNodeId":"TIT7BURE_CH3DEIMFE_ARTDPAIMFE","NodeDepth":4,"TitleHtml":"
7-3D-5: - Methodology
","ShouldShowMiniToc":false,"Id":"TIT7BURE_CH3DEIMFE_ARTDPAIMFE_7-3D-5ME","Title":"7-3D-5: - Methodology","Content":"
\n

\n A.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Basis for Formula.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The Idaho Development Impact Fee Act and subsequent analyses by the City provide the\n methodology for a reasonable and fair formula to ensure that those who benefit from\n development pay their proportionate share of the cost of system improvements needed\n to serve that development. This methodology results in a formula for the calculation\n of the Impact Fee for each type of use within a given service area that is then used\n to create the Impact Fee Schedule. (See Idaho Code §67-8207.)\n

\n

\n B.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Minimum Standards Under this Formula. The Impact Fee:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 1.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Shall not exceed a proportionate share of the costs incurred or to be incurred by\n the City in the provision of system improvements to serve new Development (see Idaho\n Code §67-8204(1) and §67-8207(1));\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 2.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Is based on actual system improvement costs or reasonable estimates of such costs\n (see Idaho Code §67-8204(1));\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 3.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Is calculated on the basis of park infrastructure within the system as applicable\n to existing development as well as new growth and development. Park infrastructure\n to maintain the existing level of service is the acceptable level of service for system\n improvements under this article (see Idaho Code §67-8204, subsections (2) and (23));\n and\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 4.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Is imposed for system improvements that are attributable to the demands on the Service\n Capacity of the System generated by the new development. (See Idaho Code §67-8204(2).)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n C.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Considerations in Determining Proportionate Share.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The proportionate share is the cost of system improvements attributable to the new\n development after the City considers and accounts for the following:\n \n

\n 1.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Any appropriate credit, offset or contribution of money, dedication of land, or construction\n of system improvements;\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n 2.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Payments reasonably anticipated to be made by or because of a new development in the\n form of user fees and debt service payments;\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n 3.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n That portion of general tax and other revenue allocated by the City to system improvements;\n and\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n 4.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n All other available sources of funding such system improvements. (See Idaho Code §67-8207(1).)\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n D.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Factors considered in determination of proportionate share.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n In determining the proportionate share of the cost of system improvements to be paid\n by the developer, the following factors shall be considered and accounted for by the\n City in the calculation of the Impact Fee:\n \n

\n 1.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The cost of existing system improvements within the service area;\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n 2.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n How existing system improvements have been financed;\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n 3.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The extent to which the new development will contribute to the cost of system improvements\n through taxation, assessment, or developer or landowner contributions, or has previously\n contributed to the cost of system improvements through developer or landowner contributions;\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n 4.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The extent to which the new development is required to contribute to the cost of existing\n system improvements in the future;\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n 5.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The extent to which the new development should be credited for providing system improvements,\n without charge to other properties within the service area;\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n 6.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Extraordinary costs, if any, incurred in serving the new development;\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n 7.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The time and price differential inherent in a fair comparison of Impact Fees paid\n at different times; and\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n 8.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The availability of other sources of funding system improvements including, but not\n limited to, user charges, general tax levies, intergovernmental transfers, and special\n taxation. The Capital Improvements Plan shall include consideration of alternative\n sources of revenue. (See Idaho Code §§67-8204 (1) and 67-8207(2).)\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n (Ord. No. 431-2026, § 1, 4-7-2026)\n

7-3D-6: - Formula for Calculating the Impact Fee
","ShouldShowMiniToc":false,"Id":"TIT7BURE_CH3DEIMFE_ARTDPAIMFE_7-3D-6FOCAIMFE","Title":"7-3D-6: - Formula for Calculating the Impact Fee","Content":"
\n

\n A.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Basic Purpose and Concept: The basic purpose of the Impact Fee and the principal concept\n of the formula is to charge each new development with its proportionate share of system\n improvement costs of new or expanding parks infrastructure under the jurisdiction\n of the City to handle the increased usage demand that will eventually result from\n all the new developments that can be expected to be built according to adopted land\n use plans.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The number and type of new developments that can be projected to be built in a geographic\n area, the residential use that can be expected from each new development, the costs\n of expanding the Service Capacity of parks infrastructure, the proportionate share,\n and the other factors that under the Idaho Development Impact Fee Act must be considered\n for inclusion in the Impact Fee formula are based on reasonable estimates and averages\n using the best available sources and applied in accordance with generally accepted\n accounting principles and engineering and planning criteria. (See Idaho Code §67-8204(23).)\n

\n

\n B.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Impact Fee Schedule: Based on the formula described in City of Star Development Impact\n Fee Analysis & Capital Improvement Plans: Parks, Pathways, Police, February 19, 2026,\n the amount of the Impact Fee for a development at the specified land use is presumed\n to be the amount set forth in the Impact Fee Schedule. See the Technical Memorandum\n attached in Exhibit \"B.\"\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (Ord. No. 431-2026, § 1, 4-7-2026)\n

","SortDate":null,"Footnotes":null},{"DocType":1,"IsAmended":false,"IsUpdated":true,"CompareStatus":0,"DocOrderId":404,"AmendedBy":[],"UncodifiedOrdinancesAffectingThis":[],"Notes":[],"Drafts":[],"ChunkGroupStartingNodeId":"TIT7BURE_CH3DEIMFE_ARTDPAIMFE","NodeDepth":4,"TitleHtml":"
7-3D-7: - Property Tax Proportionate Share Calculation
","ShouldShowMiniToc":false,"Id":"TIT7BURE_CH3DEIMFE_ARTDPAIMFE_7-3D-7PRTAPRSHCA","Title":"7-3D-7: - Property Tax Proportionate Share Calculation","Content":"
\n

\n If a developer or fee payer seeks an Impact Fee tax credit, they shall provide the\n assessed value of the property (real and personal) to the Impact Fee Administrator\n within two (2) years of payment of the Impact Fee. The Impact Fee Administrator will\n use the assessed value to calculate the total amount of future property tax credit.\n The future property tax credit will then be remitted to the developer or fee payer\n or credited against the current Impact Fee certificate.\n

\n

\n (Ord. No. 431-2026, § 1, 4-7-2026)\n

","SortDate":null,"Footnotes":null},{"DocType":1,"IsAmended":false,"IsUpdated":true,"CompareStatus":0,"DocOrderId":405,"AmendedBy":[],"UncodifiedOrdinancesAffectingThis":[],"Notes":[],"Drafts":[],"ChunkGroupStartingNodeId":"TIT7BURE_CH3DEIMFE_ARTDPAIMFE","NodeDepth":4,"TitleHtml":"
7-3D-8: - Exemptions
","ShouldShowMiniToc":false,"Id":"TIT7BURE_CH3DEIMFE_ARTDPAIMFE_7-3D-8EX","Title":"7-3D-8: - Exemptions","Content":"
\n

\n The following Development activities are exempt from the requirement to pay an Impact\n Fee:\n \n

\n A.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Rebuilding the same amount of floor space of a structure which was destroyed by fire\n or other catastrophe, providing the structure is rebuilt and ready for occupancy within\n two (2) years of its destruction;\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n B.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Remodeling or repairing a structure which does not increase the number of service\n units;\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n C.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Replacing a residential unit, including a manufactured home, with another residential\n unit on the same lot, provided that the number of Service Units does not increase;\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n D.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Placing a temporary construction trailer or office on a lot;\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n E.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Constructing an addition on a residential structure which does not increase the number\n of service units; and\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n F.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Adding uses that are typically accessory to a residential use, such as tennis courts,\n swimming pools, a clubhouse or a detached garage, unless it can be clearly demonstrated\n that the use creates a significant impact on the capacity of system improvements.\n (See Idaho Code §67-8204(20).)\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n (Ord. No. 431-2026, § 1, 4-7-2026)\n

","SortDate":null,"Footnotes":null},{"DocType":1,"IsAmended":false,"IsUpdated":true,"CompareStatus":0,"DocOrderId":406,"AmendedBy":[],"UncodifiedOrdinancesAffectingThis":[],"Notes":[],"Drafts":[],"ChunkGroupStartingNodeId":"TIT7BURE_CH3DEIMFE_ARTDPAIMFE","NodeDepth":4,"TitleHtml":"
7-3D-9: - Impact Fee Advisory Committee
","ShouldShowMiniToc":false,"Id":"TIT7BURE_CH3DEIMFE_ARTDPAIMFE_7-3D-9IMFEADCO","Title":"7-3D-9: - Impact Fee Advisory Committee","Content":"
\n

\n A.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Continuation of Existing Committee: An Impact Fee Advisory Committee was previously\n established in 2025 and the Committee is still in place. It consists of not fewer\n than five (5) members appointed by the Council and its actions and activities are\n hereby ratified and approved, and for the purposes of this article the Committee is\n hereby re-established and the members re-appointed to serve for the balance of their\n respective terms.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n B.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Composition: The Impact Fee Advisory Committee shall be composed of not fewer than\n five (5) members appointed by the Council. Two (2) or more members shall be active\n in the business of Development, building or real estate. (See Idaho Code §67-8205(2)(b).)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n C.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Advisory Capacity: The Impact Fee Advisory Committee shall serve in an advisory capacity\n and is established to:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 1.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Assist the City in adopting land use assumptions;\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 2.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Review the Capital Improvements Plan and proposed amendments and file written comments;\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 3.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Monitor and evaluate implementation of the Capital Improvements Plan;\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 4.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n File periodic reports, at least annually, with respect to the Capital Improvements\n Plan and report to the Council any perceived inequities in implementing the Plan or\n imposing the Impact Fees; and\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 5.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Advise the Council of the need to update or revise land use assumptions, the Capital\n Improvements Plan and Impact Fees. (See Idaho Code §67-8205 (3).)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n D.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n City Support: The City shall make available to the Impact Fee Advisory Committee,\n upon request, all financial and accounting information, professional reports in relation\n to other development and implementation of land use assumptions, the Capital Improvements\n Plan and periodic updates of the Capital Improvements Plan. (See Idaho Code §67-8205\n (4).)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (Ord. No. 431-2026, § 1, 4-7-2026)\n

","SortDate":null,"Footnotes":null},{"DocType":1,"IsAmended":false,"IsUpdated":true,"CompareStatus":0,"DocOrderId":407,"AmendedBy":[],"UncodifiedOrdinancesAffectingThis":[],"Notes":[],"Drafts":[],"ChunkGroupStartingNodeId":"TIT7BURE_CH3DEIMFE_ARTDPAIMFE","NodeDepth":4,"TitleHtml":"
7-3D-10: - Capital Improvements Plan
","ShouldShowMiniToc":false,"Id":"TIT7BURE_CH3DEIMFE_ARTDPAIMFE_7-3D-10CAIMPL","Title":"7-3D-10: - Capital Improvements Plan","Content":"
\n

\n A.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Adoption of Capital Improvements Plan: The City shall adopt and update the Capital\n Improvements Plan.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n B.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Contents: The Capital Improvements Plan, as referenced in Exhibit \"B'' and each update\n thereof which is adopted by the Council shall contain all of the following:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 1.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n A general description of the System and its existing deficiencies within the service\n area and a reasonable estimate of all costs of, and a plan to develop the funding\n resources related to, curing such existing deficiencies including, but not limited\n to, the upgrading, updating, improving, expanding or replacing the System to meet\n existing needs and usage;\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 2.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n A commitment by the City to use other available sources of revenue to cure existing\n System deficiencies where practical;\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 3.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n An analysis of the total Service Capacity, the level of current usage, and commitments\n for usage of the Service Capacity of existing Capital Improvements, which shall be\n prepared by a qualified professional planner or by a qualified engineer licensed to\n perform engineering services in this state;\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 4.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n A description of the land use assumptions most recently adopted by the City;\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 5.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n A definitive table establishing the specific level or quantity of use by a Development\n of system improvements and an equivalency or conversion table establishing the ratio\n of a Service Unit to various types of land uses, including residential, commercial,\n and industrial;\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 6.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n A description of all system improvements and their costs necessitated by and attributable\n to new Development in the service area based on the approved land use assumptions,\n to provide a level of service not to exceed the level of services adopted in this\n article;\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 7.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The total number of Service Units necessitated by and attributable to new developments\n within the service area based on the approved land use assumptions and calculated\n in accordance with generally accepted engineering or planning criteria;\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 8.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The projected demand for system improvements required by new Service Units projected\n over a reasonable period of time not to exceed twenty (20) years;\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 9.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Identification of all sources and levels of funding Available to the City for the\n financing of the system improvements; and\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 10.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n A schedule setting forth estimated dates for commencing and completing construction\n of all system improvements identified in the Capital Improvements Plan. (See Idaho\n Code §67-8208(1).)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n C.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Capital Improvement Plan Updates:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 1.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The City shall update the Capital Improvements Plan at least once every five (5) years,\n each update shall be made in accordance with procedures set forth in Idaho Code §67-8206.\n (See Idaho Code §67-8208(2).)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 2.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The Capital Improvements Plan shall be updated in conformance with the provisions\n of this section each time the City proposes the amendment, modification or adoption\n of a development impact fee ordinance. (See Idaho Code §67-8208(4).)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n D.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Annual Adoption of Capital Budget: The Council must annually adopt a capital budget.\n (See Idaho Code §67-8208(3).)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (Ord. No. 431-2026, § 1, 4-7-2026)\n

","SortDate":null,"Footnotes":null},{"DocType":1,"IsAmended":false,"IsUpdated":true,"CompareStatus":0,"DocOrderId":408,"AmendedBy":[],"UncodifiedOrdinancesAffectingThis":[],"Notes":[],"Drafts":[],"ChunkGroupStartingNodeId":"TIT7BURE_CH3DEIMFE_ARTDPAIMFE","NodeDepth":4,"TitleHtml":"
7-3D-11: - Fee Certification
","ShouldShowMiniToc":false,"Id":"TIT7BURE_CH3DEIMFE_ARTDPAIMFE_7-3D-11FECE","Title":"7-3D-11: - Fee Certification","Content":"
\n

\n A developer shall receive, upon request, a written certification of the Impact Fee\n or individual assessment for a particular development. The Impact Fee Administrator\n shall provide the developer with written certification of the Impact Fee for that\n Development, which shall establish the Impact Fee so long as there is no material\n change to the particular project as identified in the Individual Assessment Application,\n or change to the Impact Fee Schedule. The certification shall include an explanation\n of the calculation of the Impact Fee including an explanation of factors considered\n by the Council. The certification shall also specify the System Improvement(s) for\n which the Impact Fee is intended to be used. (See Idaho Code §67-8204(6).)\n

\n

\n (Ord. No. 431-2026, § 1, 4-7-2026)\n

","SortDate":null,"Footnotes":null},{"DocType":1,"IsAmended":false,"IsUpdated":true,"CompareStatus":0,"DocOrderId":409,"AmendedBy":[],"UncodifiedOrdinancesAffectingThis":[],"Notes":[],"Drafts":[],"ChunkGroupStartingNodeId":"TIT7BURE_CH3DEIMFE_ARTDPAIMFE","NodeDepth":4,"TitleHtml":"
7-3D-12: - Individual Assessments
","ShouldShowMiniToc":false,"Id":"TIT7BURE_CH3DEIMFE_ARTDPAIMFE_7-3D-12INAS","Title":"7-3D-12: - Individual Assessments","Content":"
\n

\n A.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Initiating an Individual Assessment:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 1.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n A developer or fee payer may provide a written individual assessment of the proportionate\n share of the Impact Fee for the proposed development. (See Idaho Code §67-8204(5).)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 2.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The individual assessment process allows the consideration of studies, data and any\n other relevant information submitted by the developer or fee payer to adjust the amount\n of the Impact Fee. (See Idaho Code §67-8204(5).)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 3.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n To initiate an individual assessment, the developer or fee payer shall submit a written\n Individual Assessment Application to the Impact Fee Administrator no later than thirty\n (30) days after the date of payment of the Impact Fee. (See Idaho Code §67-8204(14).)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 4.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The individual assessment submittal shall consist of all the required supporting documentation\n and analysis in conformance with the City policies and procedures.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 5.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n An individual assessment submittal of the Impact Fee for the proposed Development\n shall be permitted sufficiently in advance of the time the developer or fee payer\n may seek a building permit or related permits so that the issuance of a building permit\n or related development permits will not be delayed. To be approved before a building\n permit or related development permits are issued, the individual assessment submittal\n must be received by the City at such a time as to permit the Impact Fee Administrator\n to render a decision. (See Idaho Code §67-8204(14).)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 6.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The developer or fee payer shall present, and pay for the cost of supporting documentation\n and analysis for the individual assessment submittal. (See Idaho Code §67-8204(5).)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 7.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n If there is a material change to the particular project, the Impact Fee Administrator\n shall determine if the change warrants an update to the individual assessment.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 8.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The Impact Fee Administrator shall review the individual assessment submittal and\n determine if it is complete. If the Impact Fee Administrator determines that the individual\n assessment submittal is not complete, a written statement shall be sent to the developer\n or fee payer submitting the individual assessment specifying the deficiencies. The\n Impact Fee Administrator shall take no further action on the individual assessment\n submittal until the submittal is deemed complete.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 9.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n A developer or fee payer submitting an individual assessment shall pay a review fee\n to the City to cover the cost of reviewing the individual assessment submittal. The\n review fee amount shall be in accordance with the City's current fee schedule.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n B.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Assessment Procedures and Documentation:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 1.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The documentation and analysis supporting the individual assessment submittal shall\n be signed by the developer or fee payer and the individual preparing the individual\n assessment submittal.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 2.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The individual assessment submittal, prepared by the developer or fee payer, shall\n include a determination of each of the factors in the Impact Fee formula for the Development\n that is the subject of the individual assessment.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 3.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Alternative methods for determining the factors in the Impact Fee formula must be\n approved in writing by the Impact Fee Administrator prior to submitting the individual\n assessment submittal.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 4.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The individual assessment submittal shall include a calculation of the Impact Fee\n based on the facts presented, utilizing the same methodology and formula used in developing\n the Impact Fee Schedule.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n C.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Decision: The Impact Fee Administrator may accept, accept with conditions, or reject\n the documentation and analysis or require the developer or fee payer to submit additional\n or different documentation.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n No later than twenty (20) calendar days following the completion of the presentation\n of all required documentation and, after considering the same and making appropriate\n findings based thereon, the Impact Fee Administrator shall decide as to the Impact\n Fee to be charged for the development. The decision shall be based upon the requirements\n of Idaho Code §67-8207 and shall include an explanation of the calculation of the\n Impact Fee, including an explanation of factors considered under Idaho Code §67-8207,\n and shall specify the System Improvement(s) for which the Impact Fee is intended to\n be used. (See Idaho Code §67-8204(5).)\n

\n

\n D.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Appeal from Decision: If the developer or fee payer does not accept the decision of\n the Impact Fee Administrator, an appeal may be filed with the Council.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (Ord. No. 431-2026, § 1, 4-7-2026)\n

","SortDate":null,"Footnotes":null},{"DocType":1,"IsAmended":false,"IsUpdated":true,"CompareStatus":0,"DocOrderId":410,"AmendedBy":[],"UncodifiedOrdinancesAffectingThis":[],"Notes":[],"Drafts":[],"ChunkGroupStartingNodeId":"TIT7BURE_CH3DEIMFE_ARTDPAIMFE","NodeDepth":4,"TitleHtml":"
7-3D-13: - Extraordinary Impacts; Overlay Zones and Overlay Fees
","ShouldShowMiniToc":false,"Id":"TIT7BURE_CH3DEIMFE_ARTDPAIMFE_7-3D-13EXIMOVZOOVFE","Title":"7-3D-13: - Extraordinary Impacts; Overlay Zones and Overlay Fees","Content":"
\n

\n There will be situations where the anticipated impacts to the system of a proposed\n development will comprise an extraordinary impact. The Council may adopt an Extraordinary\n Impact Fee ordinance which calculates a pro rata share per parcel of the Development\n of the Extraordinary Costs. The Council may by resolution adopt an Overlay Fee equal\n to such pro rata share of the extraordinary costs in addition to the Impact Fee.\n

\n

\n (Ord. No. 431-2026, § 1, 4-7-2026)\n

","SortDate":null,"Footnotes":null},{"DocType":1,"IsAmended":false,"IsUpdated":true,"CompareStatus":0,"DocOrderId":411,"AmendedBy":[],"UncodifiedOrdinancesAffectingThis":[],"Notes":[],"Drafts":[],"ChunkGroupStartingNodeId":"TIT7BURE_CH3DEIMFE_ARTDPAIMFE","NodeDepth":4,"TitleHtml":"
7-3D-14: - Credit or Reimbursement
","ShouldShowMiniToc":false,"Id":"TIT7BURE_CH3DEIMFE_ARTDPAIMFE_7-3D-14CRRE","Title":"7-3D-14: - Credit or Reimbursement","Content":"
\n

\n A\n

\n \t\t\n

\n For Construction, Contribution, Taxes and User Fees Generated:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 1.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n In the calculation of Impact Fees for a project, credit or reimbursement shall be\n given for the present value of any construction of system improvements or dedication\n of land or money required by the City from a developer for system improvements of\n the category for which the Impact Fee is being collected, including such system improvements\n paid for pursuant to a local improvement district credit or reimbursement shall not\n be given for Project Improvements. (See Idaho Code §67-8209(1).)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 2.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n In calculation of Impact Fees for a project, credit shall be given for the present\n value of all tax and user fee revenue generated by the developer, within the service\n area where the Impact Fee is being assessed and used by the City for system improvements\n of the category for which the Impact Fee is being collected. If the amount of the\n credit exceeds the proportionate share for the project, the developer shall receive\n a credit on future Impact Fees for the amount in excess of the proportionate share.\n The credit may be applied by the developer as an offset against future Impact Fees\n only in the service area where the credit was generated. (See Idaho Code §67-8209(2).)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 3.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n If a developer is required to construct, fund or contribute system improvements in\n excess of the Development's proportionate share of system improvement costs, including\n such system improvements paid for pursuant to a local improvement district, the developer\n shall receive a credit on future Impact Fees or be reimbursed at the developer's choice\n for such excess construction, funding or contribution from Impact Fees paid by future\n development which impacts the system improvements constructed, funded or contributed\n by the developer or fee payer. (See Idaho Code §67-8209(3).)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n B.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Procedures and Documentation:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 1.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n If credit or reimbursement is due the developer pursuant to this section from the\n construction of system improvements or dedication of land or money required by the\n City, the City shall enter into a written agreement with the developer or fee payer,\n negotiated in good faith, prior to the construction, funding or contribution. The\n agreement shall provide for the amount of credit or the amount, time and form of reimbursement.\n (See Idaho Code §67-8209(4).)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 2.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n To apply for credit for the Present Value of all tax and user fee revenue generated\n by the developer within the service area where the Impact Fee is being assessed and\n used by the City for system improvements of the category for which the Impact Fee\n is being collected, the developer shall submit an application for Impact Fee credit\n and all supporting documentation to the Impact Fee Administrator within thirty (30)\n calendar days of the date of payment of the Impact Fee to which the credit is being\n applied. The Impact Fee Administrator shall determine if the developer is eligible\n for credit towards the Impact Fee and calculate the amount of the credit. If credit\n is due the developer, the credit amount will be deducted from the Impact Fee.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (Ord. No. 431-2026, § 1, 4-7-2026)\n

","SortDate":null,"Footnotes":null},{"DocType":1,"IsAmended":false,"IsUpdated":true,"CompareStatus":0,"DocOrderId":412,"AmendedBy":[],"UncodifiedOrdinancesAffectingThis":[],"Notes":[],"Drafts":[],"ChunkGroupStartingNodeId":"TIT7BURE_CH3DEIMFE_ARTDPAIMFE","NodeDepth":4,"TitleHtml":"
7-3D-15: - Changes in Units or Scope; Modular Building, Manufactured Home or Recreational Vehicle
","ShouldShowMiniToc":false,"Id":"TIT7BURE_CH3DEIMFE_ARTDPAIMFE_7-3D-15CHUNSCMOBUMAHOREVE","Title":"7-3D-15: - Changes in Units or Scope; Modular Building, Manufactured Home or Recreational Vehicle","Content":"
\n

\n A.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Change in Number of Units, Scope of Development: After payment of the Impact Fees\n or execution of an agreement for payment of Impact Fees, additional Impact Fees or\n increases in fees may not be assessed unless the number of development units increases\n or the scope or schedule of the development changes. In the event of an increase in\n the number of development units or the scope of the development changes, the additional\n development Impact Fees to be imposed are limited to the amount attributable to the\n additional Development Units or change in scope of the development. (See Idaho Code\n §67-8204(18).)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n B.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Modular Building, Manufactured Home or Recreational Vehicle: An Impact Fee will be\n assessed for installation of a modular building, manufactured home or recreational\n vehicle unless the fee payer can demonstrate by documentation such as aerial photographs,\n utility bills and tax records, either:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 1.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n That a modular building, manufactured home or recreational vehicle was legally in\n place on the lot or space prior to the effective date of this article; or\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 2.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n That an Impact Fee has been paid previously for the installation of a modular building,\n manufactured home or recreational vehicle on that same lot or space. (See Idaho Code\n §67-8204(21).)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (Ord. No. 431-2026, § 1, 4-7-2026)\n

","SortDate":null,"Footnotes":null},{"DocType":1,"IsAmended":false,"IsUpdated":true,"CompareStatus":0,"DocOrderId":413,"AmendedBy":[],"UncodifiedOrdinancesAffectingThis":[],"Notes":[],"Drafts":[],"ChunkGroupStartingNodeId":"TIT7BURE_CH3DEIMFE_ARTDPAIMFE","NodeDepth":4,"TitleHtml":"
7-3D-16: - Payment of Impact Fee
","ShouldShowMiniToc":false,"Id":"TIT7BURE_CH3DEIMFE_ARTDPAIMFE_7-3D-16PAIMFE","Title":"7-3D-16: - Payment of Impact Fee","Content":"
\n

\n A.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Place and Time of Payment: The payment of the Impact Fee and any extra fees for extraordinary\n impacts shall be made directly to the City. The Impact Fee shall be due at the time\n of the issuance of a building permit or a manufactured home installation permit or\n a similar permit, or, if no permit is required, at the time of the commencement of\n construction of the development, or as may be otherwise agreed by the developer and\n the Impact Fee Administrator. (See Idaho Code §67-8204(3).)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n B.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Election: A developer has the right to elect to pay a Development's proportionate\n share of system improvement costs by payment of Impact Fees according to the Fee Schedule\n as full and complete payment of the development's proportionate share of system improvement\n costs, except for any costs of extraordinary impact (See Idaho Code §67-8204(17).)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (Ord. No. 431-2026, § 1, 4-7-2026)\n

","SortDate":null,"Footnotes":null},{"DocType":1,"IsAmended":false,"IsUpdated":true,"CompareStatus":0,"DocOrderId":414,"AmendedBy":[],"UncodifiedOrdinancesAffectingThis":[],"Notes":[],"Drafts":[],"ChunkGroupStartingNodeId":"TIT7BURE_CH3DEIMFE_ARTDPAIMFE","NodeDepth":4,"TitleHtml":"
7-3D-17: - Service Area
","ShouldShowMiniToc":false,"Id":"TIT7BURE_CH3DEIMFE_ARTDPAIMFE_7-3D-17SEAR","Title":"7-3D-17: - Service Area","Content":"
\n

\n The service area encompasses all the area of city impact of the City of Star.\n

\n

\n (Ord. No. 431-2026, § 1, 4-7-2026)\n

","SortDate":null,"Footnotes":null},{"DocType":1,"IsAmended":false,"IsUpdated":true,"CompareStatus":0,"DocOrderId":415,"AmendedBy":[],"UncodifiedOrdinancesAffectingThis":[],"Notes":[],"Drafts":[],"ChunkGroupStartingNodeId":"TIT7BURE_CH3DEIMFE_ARTDPAIMFE","NodeDepth":4,"TitleHtml":"
7-3D-18: - Use of Funds
","ShouldShowMiniToc":false,"Id":"TIT7BURE_CH3DEIMFE_ARTDPAIMFE_7-3D-18USFU","Title":"7-3D-18: - Use of Funds","Content":"
\n

\n A.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Separate Accounts: All Impact Fees shall be maintained in one (1) or more interest-bearing\n accounts within the capital projects fund. Accounting records shall be maintained\n for each service area in which the fees are collected. Interest earned on Impact Fees\n shall be considered funds of the account on which it is earned, and not funds subject\n to Idaho Code §57-127 and shall be subject to all restrictions placed on the use of\n Impact Fees under the provisions of this article. (See Idaho Code §67-8210(1).)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n B.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Expenditure Restricted: Expenditures of Impact Fees shall be made only for the category\n of system improvements and within or for the benefit of the service area for which\n the Impact Fee was imposed as shown by the Capital Improvements Plan and as authorized\n in this article. Impact Fees shall not be used for any purpose other than to pay for\n system improvement costs to create additional system improvements to serve new growth.\n (See Idaho Code §67-8204(11) and §67-8210(2).)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n C.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Annual Report: The City shall prepare an annual report describing:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 1.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The amount of all Impact Fees collected, appropriated, or spent during the preceding\n year by service area; and\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 2.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The percentage of tax and revenues other than Impact Fees collected, appropriated\n or spent for system improvements during the preceding year by category of public facility\n and service area. (See Idaho Code §67-8210(3).)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n D.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Time to Spend Impact Fees Collected: Collected Impact Fees must be expended within\n eight years from the date they were collected, on a first-in, first-out (FIFO) basis.\n Any funds not expended within the prescribed times shall be refunded. The City may\n hold the Impact Fees for longer than eight years if the Council identifies, in writing:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 1.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n A reasonable cause why the Impact Fees should be held longer than eight years; and\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 2.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n An anticipated date by which the Impact Fees will be expended but in no event greater\n than eleven (11) years from the date they were collected. (See Idaho Code §67-8210(4).)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (Ord. No. 431-2026, § 1, 4-7-2026)\n

","SortDate":null,"Footnotes":null},{"DocType":1,"IsAmended":false,"IsUpdated":true,"CompareStatus":0,"DocOrderId":416,"AmendedBy":[],"UncodifiedOrdinancesAffectingThis":[],"Notes":[],"Drafts":[],"ChunkGroupStartingNodeId":"TIT7BURE_CH3DEIMFE_ARTDPAIMFE","NodeDepth":4,"TitleHtml":"
7-3D-19: - Refunds; A Right to Request
","ShouldShowMiniToc":false,"Id":"TIT7BURE_CH3DEIMFE_ARTDPAIMFE_7-3D-19RERIRE","Title":"7-3D-19: - Refunds; A Right to Request","Content":"
\n

\n A.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n A refund of an Impact Fee paid under this article shall be made upon the request of\n the current owner(s) of property on which the fee has been paid if:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n A.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The request for a refund is received by the City no later than two (2) years from\n the date of payment of the Impact Fee; and\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 1.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Service is available but never provided; or\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 2.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n A building permit or permit for installation of a manufactured home or similar permit\n is denied or abandoned; or\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 3.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n After collecting the fee when service is not available, the City has failed to appropriate\n and expend the collected Impact Fees pursuant to this article (see Idaho Code §67-8211(1));\n or\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 4.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Action by the Council determines that the Impact Fee was calculated incorrectly in\n favor of the City or as a result of an appeal or mediation a refund is due; or\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 5.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The fee payer pays the Impact Fee under protest, and a subsequent review of the Impact\n Fee paid or the completion of an individual assessment determines that the Impact\n Fee paid exceeded the proportionate share to which the City was entitled to receive.\n (See Idaho Code §67-8211(d).)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n B.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Time of Payment: When the right to a refund exists under this Section, the Impact\n Fee Administrator shall send the refund to the owner of record within ninety (90)\n days after the Impact Fee Administrator has determined that a refund is due. (See\n Idaho Code §67-8211(2).)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n C.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Interest: A refund shall include a refund of interest from the date of payment of\n the Impact Fee at one-half (1/2) the legal rate provided for in Idaho Code §28-22-104(1)\n from the date of which the fee was originally paid. (See Idaho Code §67-8211(3).)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n D.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Standing: Any Person entitled to a refund shall have standing to sue for a refund\n under the provisions of Idaho Development Impact Fee Act if there has not been a timely\n payment of a refund. (Reference Idaho Code, Section 67-8211(4).) (Reference Idaho\n Code, Section 67-8204(12).)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (Ord. No. 431-2026, § 1, 4-7-2026)\n

","SortDate":null,"Footnotes":null},{"DocType":1,"IsAmended":false,"IsUpdated":true,"CompareStatus":0,"DocOrderId":417,"AmendedBy":[],"UncodifiedOrdinancesAffectingThis":[],"Notes":[],"Drafts":[],"ChunkGroupStartingNodeId":"TIT7BURE_CH3DEIMFE_ARTDPAIMFE","NodeDepth":4,"TitleHtml":"
7-3D-20: - Loans to Service Area Fund; Extraordinary Impact Loans
","ShouldShowMiniToc":false,"Id":"TIT7BURE_CH3DEIMFE_ARTDPAIMFE_7-3D-20LOSEARFUEXIMLO","Title":"7-3D-20: - Loans to Service Area Fund; Extraordinary Impact Loans","Content":"
\n

\n A.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Loans to Service Area Fund: The Council may loan funds held by it in its general accounts\n to a service area capital projects fund where the fund does not have sufficient balances\n to pay all of the system improvement costs to be incurred for the construction of\n a System Improvement in that service area. As Impact Fees are generated and collected\n in that service area, the loan will be repaid, without interest, by the transfer of\n funds from the capital projects fund for that service area to the general accounts\n of the City.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n B.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Council Resolution Required: The making of any such loan shall require the adoption\n of a resolution by the Council at a regular or special meeting.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (Ord. No. 431-2026, § 1, 4-7-2026)\n

","SortDate":null,"Footnotes":null},{"DocType":1,"IsAmended":false,"IsUpdated":true,"CompareStatus":0,"DocOrderId":418,"AmendedBy":[],"UncodifiedOrdinancesAffectingThis":[],"Notes":[],"Drafts":[],"ChunkGroupStartingNodeId":"TIT7BURE_CH3DEIMFE_ARTDPAIMFE","NodeDepth":4,"TitleHtml":"
7-3D-21: - Administrative Appeals
","ShouldShowMiniToc":false,"Id":"TIT7BURE_CH3DEIMFE_ARTDPAIMFE_7-3D-21ADAP","Title":"7-3D-21: - Administrative Appeals","Content":"
\n

\n A.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Appeal to Council; Grounds: The Council shall hear and decide appeals by any developer,\n fee payer or property owner aggrieved by a final decision made by the Impact Fee Administrator\n under this article where it is alleged that the Impact Fee Administrator did not properly\n apply this article, did not consider all relevant facts presented, abused discretion\n or acted arbitrarily and capriciously in the interpretation or enforcement of this\n article.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n B.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Filing Fee: The fee for filing an appeal shall be in accordance with the City's current\n fee schedule.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n C.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Initiation: An appeal is initiated by the filing of a written notice of appeal together\n with the filing fee with the City, which must be filed within thirty (30) calendar\n days from the date of the final decision that is the subject of the appeal. If the\n thirtieth day falls on a weekend or holiday, the notice of appeal may be filed the\n following business day. The notice of appeal shall refer to the decision being appealed,\n identify the appellant by name, address and telephone number and state the grounds\n for the appeal. The grounds shall include a written summary of the provisions of the\n article relevant to the appeal and/or the facts relied upon and shall include a written\n argument in support of the appeal. A notice of appeal that does not comply with the\n provisions of this subparagraph shall not be considered by the Council, and no further\n action with respect thereto shall be taken under this section.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n D.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Time to Reply: The Impact Fee Administrator shall have fourteen (14) calendar days\n to reply to the notice of appeal and may during such time meet with the appellant\n to discuss the matter and may also reconsider and/or amend the decision which is being\n appealed. A copy of the reply, and any amendments or supplements to the decision being\n appealed from will be provided to the appellant prior to the hearing on the appeal.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n E.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Notice of Hearing: Unless otherwise agreed to by the appellant, the hearing on the\n appeal will be noticed and scheduled for a regular meeting of the Council to be held\n within thirty (30) calendar days following the delivery to the appellant of the Impact\n Fee Administrator's reply to the notice of appeal. A copy of the decision being appealed,\n the notice of appeal and the reply shall be delivered to the Council prior to the\n hearing.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n F.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Action by Council: After the hearing, the Council may reverse or affirm, in whole\n or in part, or otherwise modify, amend or supplement the decision being appealed,\n as such action is adequately supported by the evidence and testimony presented at\n the hearing.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n G.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Payment Under Protest: A fee payer may pay an Impact Fee under protest in order to\n obtain a development approval or a building permit. A fee payer making such payment\n shall not be estopped from exercising the right of appeal provided in this section,\n nor shall such fee payer be estopped from receiving a refund of any amount deemed\n to have been improperly collected as a result of the appeal. (See Idaho Code §67-8212(2).)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n H.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Mediation: Upon voluntary agreement by the fee payer and the Impact Fee Administrator,\n the City shall address a disagreement related to the Impact Fee for a proposed development\n through mediation by a qualified independent party. Mediation may take place at any\n time during the appeals process and participation in mediation does not preclude the\n fee payer from pursuing other remedies provided for in this Section. Mediation costs\n will be shared equally by the fee payer and the City. (See Idaho Code §67-8204(15)\n and §67-8212(3).)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (Ord. No. 431-2026, § 1, 4-7-2026)\n

","SortDate":null,"Footnotes":null},{"DocType":1,"IsAmended":false,"IsUpdated":true,"CompareStatus":0,"DocOrderId":419,"AmendedBy":[],"UncodifiedOrdinancesAffectingThis":[],"Notes":[],"Drafts":[],"ChunkGroupStartingNodeId":"TIT7BURE_CH3DEIMFE_ARTDPAIMFE","NodeDepth":4,"TitleHtml":"
7-3D-22: - Collection
","ShouldShowMiniToc":false,"Id":"TIT7BURE_CH3DEIMFE_ARTDPAIMFE_7-3D-22CO","Title":"7-3D-22: - Collection","Content":"
\n

\n If a fee payer fails to pay an Impact Fee when due, in addition to such other remedies\n as are available to the City at law or in equity to collect the same, the City may\n do one or more of the following:\n \n

\n A.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Withhold building permit or other approvals until the Impact Fee is paid;\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n B.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Direct the withholding of utility services until the Impact Fee is paid;\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n C.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Charge the developer interest on the Impact Fee at the legal rate set forth in Idaho\n Code §28-22-104 (1), from the date such payment was due until paid;\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n D.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Charge a penalty for failure to pay an Impact Fee when due in an amount of five percent\n (5%) of the Impact Fee for each month elapsing after the date the fee was due until\n paid, such penalty not to exceed twenty-five percent (25%) of the fee;\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n E.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Impose a lien on the lot or parcel upon which the Development is occurring for failure\n to timely pay the Impact Fee in the amount of the Impact Fee and such costs, penalties\n and interest as are allowable, by following the procedures contained in Idaho Code,\n Chapter 5, Title 45. (See Idaho Code §67-8213.)\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n (Ord. No. 431-2026, § 1, 4-7-2026)\n

","SortDate":null,"Footnotes":null},{"DocType":1,"IsAmended":false,"IsUpdated":true,"CompareStatus":0,"DocOrderId":420,"AmendedBy":[],"UncodifiedOrdinancesAffectingThis":[],"Notes":[],"Drafts":[],"ChunkGroupStartingNodeId":"TIT7BURE_CH3DEIMFE_ARTDPAIMFE","NodeDepth":4,"TitleHtml":"
7-3D-23: - Guidelines
","ShouldShowMiniToc":false,"Id":"TIT7BURE_CH3DEIMFE_ARTDPAIMFE_7-3D-23GU","Title":"7-3D-23: - Guidelines","Content":"
\n

\n The Council may adopt guidelines, interpretations and forms consistent with this article\n to implement its intent.\n

\n

\n (Ord. No. 431-2026, § 1, 4-7-2026)\n

","SortDate":null,"Footnotes":null},{"DocType":1,"IsAmended":false,"IsUpdated":true,"CompareStatus":0,"DocOrderId":421,"AmendedBy":[],"UncodifiedOrdinancesAffectingThis":[],"Notes":[],"Drafts":[],"ChunkGroupStartingNodeId":"TIT7BURE_CH3DEIMFE_ARTDPAIMFE","NodeDepth":4,"TitleHtml":"
7-3D-24: - Other Powers and Rights not Affected
","ShouldShowMiniToc":false,"Id":"TIT7BURE_CH3DEIMFE_ARTDPAIMFE_7-3D-24OTPORINOAF","Title":"7-3D-24: - Other Powers and Rights not Affected","Content":"
\n

\n A.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Project Improvements: Nothing in this article shall prevent the City from requiring\n a developer to construct reasonable Project improvements in conjunction with a development.\n (See Idaho Code §67-8214(1).)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n B.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n No Obligation to Approve Developments with Extraordinary Impacts: Nothing in this\n article shall obligate the City to approve Development which results in an extraordinary\n impact. (See Idaho Code §67-8214(3).)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n C.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n No Obligation to Approve Below Acceptable Level of Service: Nothing in this article\n shall obligate the City to approve any request for development approval which may\n reasonably be expected to reduce existing levels of service. (See Idaho Code §67-8214(4).)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n D.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n No Limitation on Power of Eminent Domain, Creation of Local Improvement Districts\n or Bond Issues: Nothing in this article shall work to limit the use by the City of\n the power of eminent domain or supersede or conflict with requirements or procedures\n authorized in Idaho Code for local improvement districts or general obligation bond\n issues. (See Idaho Code §67-8214(6).)\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (Ord. No. 431-2026, § 1, 4-7-2026)\n

7-3D-25: - Review
","ShouldShowMiniToc":false,"Id":"TIT7BURE_CH3DEIMFE_ARTDPAIMFE_7-3D-25RE","Title":"7-3D-25: - Review","Content":"
\n

\n In connection with each update of the Capital Improvement Plan, and more often at\n the discretion of the Council, the Impact Fee Administrator shall review the Fee Schedule\n and the relevant factors on which it is based, in coordination with the Impact Fee\n Advisory Committee. Based upon this review, the Impact Fee Administrator may recommend\n to the Council a revision of this article, including the Fee Schedule.\n

\n

\n (Ord. No. 431-2026, § 1, 4-7-2026)\n

7-3D-26: - Errors in Formula
","ShouldShowMiniToc":false,"Id":"TIT7BURE_CH3DEIMFE_ARTDPAIMFE_7-3D-26ERFO","Title":"7-3D-26: - Errors in Formula","Content":"
\n

\n If the City discovers an error in the Impact Fee formula that results in assessment\n or payment of more than a proportionate share the City shall, at the time of assessment,\n on a case by case basis adjust the fee to collect no more than a proportionate share\n or the City shall discontinue the collection of any Impact Fees until the error is\n corrected by ordinance. (See Idaho Code §67-8213.)\n

\n

\n (Ord. No. 431-2026, § 1, 4-7-2026)\n
